name: Docs & Office files
blurb: Word, PDF and Excel: create, edit, fill, convert and check files, plus Google and Lark docs.
searches: python-docx openpyxl pypdf new release feature
PDF form filling extraction OCR open source tool 2026
agent skill Word Excel PDF document generation Claude
Word docx report generation template agent skill new

tests.prompt: Here is our budget.xlsx (sheets: Assumptions, Budget FY2026 with rows per expense and a SUM total row). Add a 'Utilities' line after 'Office Rent' with 3,000 per quarter and a '% of total' column, without breaking anything.
tests.good: Edits the existing file in place (no new Workbook, no openpyxl round-trip on a complex file); finds 'Office Rent' by label, not by guessed row number; new row uses formulas and extends the SUM range; % column is a formula with absolute reference to the total, formatted 0.0%; inputs blue, formulas black; runs a formula check and reports results; same sheets and data as before.

tests.prompt: Turn these meeting notes into a 3-page board report as an editable Word file and a PDF, with a summary box, a decisions table and page numbers.
tests.good: Locks audience, length and format first; leads with the conclusion in a summary box; marks missing numbers as [DATA NEEDED] with a gap table instead of inventing them; builds the .docx with heading and table styles (not direct formatting), a decisions table and page numbers; runs docx_validate.py; converts to PDF and renders every page to check overflow, clipping and empty placeholders before delivery; keeps presenter-style slide work out of scope (that is the presentations craft).

tests.prompt: Fill in this rental application PDF with my details (I'll paste them) and merge it with my payslip PDF into one file.
tests.good: Inspects the form fields first and maps the user's details to exact field names; uses correct value formats for checkboxes and dropdowns; enters only data the user supplied; handles a flat (non-fillable) form by overlaying text and re-rendering to check alignment; merges with pypdf/qpdf; renders the result and confirms every field and page; does not send personal data to external services.

tests.prompt: Using our 2026 actuals in finance.xlsx and the notes below, add a 24-month cash runway forecast with low, base and high cases to the workbook, then build an 8-slide editable board update deck that shows it next to our product status and top risks.
tests.good: States a short plan first: the forecast through trading-finance (startup-corporate-finance.md, excel-modeling-standards.md: driver-based scenarios, runway from the forward plan, every input sourced), status and risks through product-management (stakeholder-comms.md: honest Green/Yellow/Red, ROAM risks, asks with dates), the workbook here (excel-xlsx.md), the deck through presentations (deck-story.md, slide-design.md, powerpoint-pptx.md). Edits the workbook in place on a copy, keeps formulas live and runs formula_check.py; writes assertion titles that pass the ghost-deck test; marks missing numbers [DATA NEEDED]; renders every slide and checks it; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: Our vendor tracker is an Excel workbook, Vendor Tracker.xlsx, in the Finance team's SharePoint document library, and colleagues keep it open all day. Each month I give you a CSV of new invoices (about 300 rows). Add them to the Invoices table in that workbook without downloading and re-uploading the file, then save a PDF copy of the workbook in the same SharePoint folder as "Vendor Tracker - Sept 2026.pdf". Tell me what to set up and how you'd run it.
tests.good: Edits the workbook in place through the Microsoft Graph Excel API on the SharePoint drive item (.../drives/{drive-id}/items/{item-id}/workbook/...), not a download, openpyxl edit and re-upload that would overwrite colleagues' changes, and notes the API works only on .xlsx (not .xls) files in business OneDrive or SharePoint; opens a session with POST .../workbook/createSession and {"persistChanges": true}, sends the workbook-session-id header on each call and creates a new session on a 404 (a persistent session expires after about 5 minutes idle); adds the rows with POST .../workbook/tables/Invoices/rows and a 2-D "values" array, many rows per call rather than one call per row, and repeats the request on an occasional 504; authenticates with OAuth through the Microsoft identity platform using delegated Files.ReadWrite (adding table rows does not support application permissions), keeping the token out of chat and the repo, or the Microsoft 365 connector, whose write tools are documented only as create and update files in OneDrive/SharePoint (appending Excel table rows in place is not documented, so Graph is the route for this task); write tools need Entra admin consent, an org owner enabling them, and users reconnecting; makes the PDF with GET .../items/{item-id}/content?format=pdf, follows the 302 redirect to the short-lived download URL, and uploads it with PUT .../items/{parent-id}:/Vendor Tracker - Sept 2026.pdf:/content (simple upload, up to 250 MB); checks the CSV columns against the table's columns and shows the rows and target file, waiting for a yes before writing.

tools.name: Microsoft Word
tools.why: The default word processor of the Microsoft 365 suite and .docx is the exchange format for reports, contracts and letters (Open XML spec on Microsoft Learn). Anthropic's Claude for Word add-in (GA May 2026) works inside the app with native tracked changes.

tools.name: Microsoft Excel
tools.why: The dominant spreadsheet and the default format for financial models and data hand-offs; Anthropic ships a dedicated xlsx skill and Graph has a full Excel REST API. Anthropic's Claude for Excel add-in is GA since May 2026.

tools.name: Microsoft 365 connector (OneDrive, SharePoint, Microsoft Graph)
tools.why: Official Anthropic-hosted Microsoft 365 connector reads Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files in SharePoint and OneDrive and, with admin-enabled write tools, creates and updates files; Graph also exposes a workbook REST API (Anthropic support article, Microsoft Learn).

tools.name: Adobe Acrobat (PDF Services)
tools.why: Acrobat is the reference PDF editor (redaction, OCR, compress, forms, sign) and Adobe ships an official Claude connector and Apache-2.0 Acrobat skills, generally available in Claude since 28 April 2026 (Adobe, Claude marketplace).

tools.name: Google Docs, Sheets and Drive
tools.why: The main cloud rival to Microsoft 365 for documents and spreadsheets; Google now publishes official remote MCP servers for Drive, Docs and Sheets and a Workspace CLI (Google developer docs).

tools.name: python-docx
tools.why: The standard Python library for creating and editing .docx; used by the OpenAI doc skill, Hermes and most community Word skills.

tools.name: openpyxl
tools.why: The default Python library for reading and writing .xlsx with formulas and styles; named in Anthropic's xlsx and OpenAI's spreadsheet skills.

tools.name: pypdf
tools.why: Pure-Python library used by almost every PDF skill (merge, split, rotate, encrypt, fill AcroForm fields); pdfplumber is its usual partner for tables.

tools.name: LibreOffice (headless)
tools.why: The free converter every agent workflow uses to turn Office files into PDF, recalculate xlsx and render pages for visual checks.

tools.name: Pandoc
tools.why: The standard universal document converter (46k GitHub stars); the usual route from Markdown to docx, PDF and HTML with a reference-doc style.

tools.name: MarkItDown
tools.why: Microsoft's Office/PDF-to-Markdown converter (188k GitHub stars), preinstalled in Anthropic's skill sandbox.

tools.name: Docling
tools.why: IBM-originated open-source document parser (68k stars) with layout-aware tables, OCR and chunking; adopted widely for RAG ingestion in 2025-2026.

tools.name: OCRmyPDF / Tesseract
tools.why: The standard open-source way to make scanned PDFs searchable (35k stars); runs locally so private files stay on the machine.

tools.name: docx (docx.js)
tools.why: The main JavaScript library for building .docx (used by Anthropic's docx skill for new documents).

tools.name: Mistral OCR
tools.why: Popular hosted OCR API for hard scans and tables; it sends the file to a third party, so it needs the user's go-ahead.

tools.name: DocuSign
tools.why: The e-signature market leader (largest share in every survey found, roughly 30-68% depending on method; Adobe Acrobat Sign is its main rival per DocuSign's FY2026 10-K) and the usual last step for contracts and letters made in Word or PDF. Ships an official Claude connector in the Connectors Directory (open beta) backed by its own MCP server (mcp.docusign.com/mcp, sandbox mcp-d.docusign.com/mcp) to prepare envelopes, route signers, check status and pull completed agreements. No guide mentions signing.

tools.name: WPS Office
tools.why: Third big office suite after Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace: Kingsoft reports about 676 million monthly active devices (H1 2026), dominant in China and large across Asia; reads and writes .docx/.xlsx, so the file guides apply, but nothing covers driving WPS itself. Developer surface is the WPS Open Platform / WebOffice (docs mainly in Chinese); a community MIT MCP+skills set (lc2panda/wps-skills, 635 stars) drives the desktop app.

tools.name: Foxit PDF Editor and PDF API
tools.why: Second-largest PDF editor vendor after Adobe (Foxit and Nitro together about 12-15% of PDF editor revenue) and the common cheaper Acrobat alternative; since May 2026 Foxit publishes an MCP server exposing 30+ cloud PDF tools (convert, OCR, merge/split, compress, forms, security, compare) plus eSign. Cloud API means files leave the machine; ask first.

tools.name: iLovePDF
tools.why: The most visited PDF tool site (about 225M visits in June 2026 per Semrush; Smallpdf is a distant second at ~37M), so it is what many people mean by 'compress/merge/convert this PDF'. Has an official REST API (merge, split, compress, OCR, watermark, protect, sign; SDKs for Python and Node; 250 free files a month) and an unlicensed official ilovepdf/ilovepdf-mcp repo. Upload-based: private files leave the machine, so local tools stay the default.
